notes: Claude Code draws a spinner line with an elapsed time and an 'esc to interrupt' hint while it works, a numbered list when it needs an answer, and a prompt box with a '>' when it is waiting for a task. It also writes its state into the terminal title, which is the signal to trust: nothing a person types into the prompt can appear there.

rules.note: The title carries the spinner glyph while a turn is running. Braille covers older releases, the half-circles the newer busy spinner.
Outranks title-working: a title that says both is a turn that stopped to ask.
The screen half of the same signal, for releases and terminals where the title is not set.

Claude leaves the spinner frame on screen under a question it has just asked. Without the guards this reports 'working' for a session that is in fact stuck, which is the one failure the sidebar exists to prevent.
A finished turn, before the prompt box comes back.
The prompt box with nothing happening. It is also on screen mid-turn, hence the lower priority and the guard.
